result_text:
Template literals are now normalized like the other string literals when units are compared for duplication. The change is one line in `codeanalyzer/src/main/java/nl/obren/sokrates/sourcecode/units/CStyleHeuristicUnitsExtractor.java`, in `extraCleanContent`:

```java
cleanedContent = cleanedContent.replaceAll("`.*?`", "``");
```

It sits after the single-quote rule and before the slash rule. JavaScript and TypeScript inherit this method, so `` `Hello alpha ${name}` `` and `` `Hello beta ${name}` `` both normalize to ``` `` ```. Code outside the literals is untouched, so differences there still keep units apart.

I also added `cleanContentTemplateLiterals` to `codeanalyzer/src/test/java/nl/obren/sokrates/sourcecode/units/CStyleHeuristicUnitsExtractorTest.java`. It checks that two template literals differing only in their text normalize to the same string.

Tests run offline in the `codeanalyzer` module: `CStyleHeuristicUnitsExtractorTest`, `JavaScriptHeuristicUnitsExtractorTest`, `JavaScriptAnalyzerTest`, `DuplicationEngineTest` and `DuplicationUtilsTest`. All pass.

Limitations:
- I did not run an end-to-end check that two such JavaScript functions appear in the Duplication report. The test covers the normalization step only.
- The rule matches within one line, like the existing quote rules. A template literal that spans several lines still has its content counted.

Nothing is committed.
